subtype: Helping a parent who is targeted [Observer]
passage:
Sunday night
I came home at four and found Papa sitting straight at the dining table, phone propped on the fruit bowl, a man in uniform on the screen. Papa put a finger to his lips. His face was grey.
On a notepad he had written: police case, do not tell family, transfer FD.
I didn't shout. I sat beside him, took his hand, and wrote under his note: Papa, this is a scam. Real police never do this. Let me.
He looked at me for a long moment, then nodded. I ended the call. His hands were shaking. He kept saying, "Forty years with a clean record, and they said I'm a criminal."
I told him he had done nothing wrong, that these people fool doctors and judges too. Then we called the cybercrime helpline together, and the bank. Nothing had gone out.
He fell asleep on the sofa by eight. I keep checking on him.
Kashish

qa.q: Where was Papa's phone propped?
qa.a: Papa's phone was propped on the fruit bowl.

qa.q: What was Papa feeling when he kept repeating his clean record?
qa.a: He felt shocked and ashamed, hurt that anyone could call him a criminal after forty years.

qa.q: Which of Kashish's choices helped most?
qa.a: Staying calm, writing a quiet note instead of shouting, ending the call, and calling the cybercrime helpline and the bank together without blaming Papa.

qa.q: What might it have been like for Papa to read Kashish's note?
qa.a: It likely brought relief along with some embarrassment, giving him permission to break the silence he had been ordered to keep.

grounding: An adult child finds Papa on a long fake-police call, ordered to stay silent and move money, ends it calmly and reports it without blame.

subtype: Helping a parent who is targeted [Observer]
passage:
In the small town of Jalgaon, Abhinav got home from work early and found his father on the sofa, phone held up, sweating, whispering, "Yes, sir. Yes, sir."
On the screen was a man in a police uniform. His father's passbook and a notepad lay open on the table.
"Papa, who is it?"
His father waved him away frantically. The man on the screen said sharply, "Who is there? You were told to stay alone."
Abhinav's heart jumped, but he kept his voice calm. He sat beside his father and gently took the phone. "Papa, real police don't do this on video." He ended the call.
His father was shaking. "They said I was in a money laundering case. That if I told you, you'd be arrested too. I was about to transfer the FD money."
"You did nothing wrong, Papa. They're very clever."
His younger brother Akash brought water. Together they called the cybercrime helpline and blocked the number.

qa.q: What lay open on the table?
qa.a: His father's passbook and a notepad.

qa.q: How did Abhinav feel when he saw his father on the call?
qa.a: Abhinav felt alarmed, his heart jumping, but he stayed calm so his father wouldn't panic further.

qa.q: What did Abhinav do that protected his father?
qa.a: He calmly took the phone and ended the call, reassured his father without blame, and with Akash called the cybercrime helpline.

qa.q: How did Abhinav's father feel during and after the call?
qa.a: His father felt terrified and trapped, sweating and shaking, fearing his sons would be arrested if he told them.

grounding: It shows a son finding his father on a fake police call, staying calm, ending the call and reporting it without blaming him.

passage:
In Osaka, Kaito stopped by his grandmother's apartment on his way back from work, as he did every Thursday. She was at the kitchen table, bent over her phone, whispering, "Hai, hai."
A voice on speaker said it was the police. Her bank card had been used in a crime. She must not tell anyone. An officer would come to collect her cards and cash "for safekeeping."
Kaito's stomach dropped. His colleague Jamal had told him about this exact trick last month.
He knelt beside her and said softly, "Obaachan, may I?" He took the phone, said, "We'll call the police station ourselves," and hung up.
She looked ashamed. "They said you'd be in trouble if I told you."
"You're not in trouble. I'm not in trouble. They're very good at scaring people." He made her tea, then called the local police station's official number and reported it. An officer came that evening, a real one, and thanked her for letting her grandson help.

qa.q: What did the caller say an officer would collect?
qa.a: Her cards and cash "for safekeeping."

qa.q: How did Kaito feel when he realised what was happening?
qa.a: Kaito felt alarmed, his stomach dropping, but he stayed gentle and calm.

qa.q: What did Kaito do that helped his grandmother?
qa.a: He calmly took the phone and hung up, reassured her without blame, made tea, and reported it to the local police's official number.

qa.q: How did Kaito's grandmother feel after the call?
qa.a: She felt ashamed and frightened, believing Kaito would be in trouble because she told him.

grounding: It shows a grandson finding his grandmother on a fake police call, staying calm, ending it and reporting it without blaming her.

At the bank branch near the market, Hemant was waiting in line to deposit a cheque when he saw his uncle, Jagdish Chacha, at the counter, phone on video call, telling the clerk, "Transfer all of it. Quickly. It's urgent."
The man on the screen was in uniform. Hemant heard him say, "Don't tell the clerk why."
Hemant's heart pounded. He walked over calmly. "Chacha, namaste. Who's this?"
Jagdish Chacha's eyes were full of fear. "Police. They say I'm in a case. I must pay to clear my name. They said not to tell family."
Hemant gently took the phone and ended the call. "Chacha, real police never do this on video. You haven't done anything wrong."
The clerk nodded; she had seen three cases this month. She stopped the transfer. Hemant sat his uncle down with water, and together, from the branch manager's office, they called the cybercrime helpline.

qa.q: What did Jagdish Chacha tell the clerk to do?
qa.a: Transfer all of it. Quickly.

qa.q: How did Hemant feel when he saw his uncle at the counter?
qa.a: Hemant felt alarmed, his heart pounding, but he walked over calmly so as not to frighten his uncle.

qa.q: What did Hemant do that fits the right response?
qa.a: He calmly ended the call, reassured his uncle without blame, and with the bank staff stopped the transfer and called the cybercrime helpline.

qa.q: How did Jagdish Chacha feel during the call?
qa.a: He felt fearful and pressured, believing he was in a police case and must not tell family.

grounding: It shows a nephew finding his uncle on a fake police call at the bank, staying calm, ending the call and reporting it without blame.

subtype: Helping a parent who is targeted [Observer]
passage:
Dear Sarita,
I need to tell you what happened with Papa yesterday, before you hear it from him and worry.
I came home early and found him in his room, door shut, on a video call. A man in a police uniform was telling him to stay silent and not speak to anyone in the house. Papa's face was grey. His chequebook was on the bed and the banking app was already open.
I didn't shout. I sat next to him, took his hand and said, "Papa, I'm here." Then I ended the call. He kept saying sorry, sorry, that they knew his full name and address. I told him, "You did nothing wrong. They do this to thousands of people."
We rang the cybercrime helpline together and reported it. Nothing was sent, thank God.
Please call him tonight, but don't scold him. He's embarrassed enough.
Love,
Payal

qa.q: What did the man in uniform tell Papa to do?
qa.a: To stay silent and not speak to anyone in the house.

qa.q: What does Payal's quiet approach suggest about Payal's feelings?
qa.a: Payal was likely alarmed but chose to stay calm, taking Papa's hand instead of shouting so he would not feel more frightened.

qa.q: Why does Payal ask Sarita not to scold Papa?
qa.a: Because Papa is already embarrassed; blame could make him hide the next call, while kindness keeps him willing to tell them.

qa.q: What was the call like for Papa?
qa.a: Papa was frightened, his face grey and ready to pay, and then ashamed, saying sorry again and again.

grounding: Shows a family member finding an older parent on a long call told to stay silent, staying calm, ending the call, reporting it and not blaming him.
